Description

Cholesterol can control ERK from outside the membrane, through the oxysterol-binding protein OSBP. In the cytosol OSBP binds cholesterol and forms an oligomer of about 440 kDa with a tyrosine phosphatase of the PTPPBS family and the serine/threonine phosphatase PP2A. Together the two phosphatases remove both phosphates of active ERK. When cholesterol in the cell falls, or when oxysterols bind OSBP, the oligomer comes apart and phosphorylated ERK rises, and more OSBP oligomer lowers the basal level of phosphorylated ERK [1]. This rests on one study and is shown as a context variant.

References

  1. Wang PY, Weng J, Anderson RG. OSBP is a cholesterol-regulated scaffolding protein in control of ERK 1/2 activation. Science. 2005;307(5714):1472-6. PMID: 15746430. doi: 10.1126/science.1107710.
